abstract: <jats:p>The periodic breakdowns of stripe rust resistance due to emergence of new virulent and more aggressive pathotypes of<jats:italic>Puccinia striiformis</jats:italic>f. sp.<jats:italic>tritici</jats:italic>have resulted in severe epidemics in India. This necessitates the search for new and more durable resistance sources against stripe rust. The three bread wheat cultivars PBW 343 (carries<jats:italic>Yr9</jats:italic>and<jats:italic>Yr27</jats:italic>), PBW 621 (carries<jats:italic>Yr17</jats:italic>) and HD 2967 (gene not known) were highly popular among the farmers after their release in 2011. But presently all three cultivars are highly susceptible to stripe rust at seedling as well as at adult plant stages as their resistance has been broken down due to emergence of new pathotypes of the pathogen (110S119, 238S119). In previous study, the crosses of PBW 621 with PBW 343 and HD 2967 and evaluation of further generations (up to F<jats:sub>4</jats:sub>) against pathotype 78S84 resulted in resistant segregants. In the present study, the F<jats:sub>5</jats:sub>and F<jats:sub>6</jats:sub>RIL populations have been evaluated against new pathotypes of<jats:italic>Pst</jats:italic>. The RILs categorized based on the disease severity on the P (Penultimate leaf) and F (flag) leaf into three categories i.e., high, moderate and low level of APR (adult plant resistance) having 1–200, 201–400 and >400 values of AUDPC, respectively, upon infection with stripe rust. The various APR components (latent period, lesion growth rate, spore production and uredial density) were studied on each category, i.e., resistant, moderately resistant and susceptible. The values of APR parameters decreased as the level of resistance increased. Based on molecular analysis, the lines (representing different categories of cross PBW 621 X PBW 343) containing the genes<jats:italic>Yr9</jats:italic>and<jats:italic>Yr17</jats:italic>due to their interactive effect provide resistance. Based on BSA using 35k SNPs and KASP markers association with phenotypic data of the RIL population (PBW 621 X HD 2967) showed the presence of two QTLs (<jats:italic>Q</jats:italic>.<jats:italic>Pst</jats:italic>.<jats:italic>pau-6B</jats:italic>,<jats:italic>Q</jats:italic>.<jats:italic>Pst</jats:italic>.<jats:italic>pau-5B</jats:italic>) responsible for the residual resistance and two SNPs AX-94891670 and AX-94454107 were found to be associated with the trait of interest on chromosome 6B and 5B respectively. The present study concludes that in the population of both the crosses (PBW 621 X PBW 343 and PBW 621 X HD 2967) major defeated gene contributed towards residual resistance by interacting with minor gene/QTLs.</jats:p>
